headline: Vaccines teach your immune system to fight enemies it's never met
universal_truth: Preparation beats reaction; training before battle determines the outcome
fun_facts: Smallpox killed an estimated 500 million people in the 20th century alone—vaccines eliminated it entirely
Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine in 1796 using cowpox to prevent smallpox
Your immune system has memory cells that can remember threats for decades
discussion_questions: How is a vaccine different from medicine?
Why do some vaccines need boosters?
What diseases might we eliminate with vaccines in the future?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your immune system is smart—once it defeats an enemy, it remembers. Next time that enemy appears, it's destroyed before you even feel sick. Vaccines hack this system, introducing harmless versions of threats so your body learns to fight them in advance.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If vaccines contain parts of diseases, why don't they make you sick? How can introducing a threat train your immune system without causing the disease itself?
cliff.prompt: How do vaccines train without infecting?

options.text: They use weakened, killed, or partial versions of pathogens—enough to trigger learning without causing disease
options.response: Yes. Vaccines show your immune system what to fight without giving it a real battle. It's like training with a practice target instead of live ammunition.

options.text: Vaccines contain antibodies that do the fighting for you
options.response: That's a different treatment. Vaccines teach your body to make its own antibodies...

q1.title: Immune Memory
q1.script: Your immune system creates 'memory cells' after fighting infections. These cells remember specific enemies for years or decades. Vaccines trigger this memory creation without requiring you to suffer through the actual disease.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Immune Memory"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Smallpox Victory
q2.script: Smallpox killed hundreds of millions. In 1796, Edward Jenner showed that cowpox infection prevented smallpox. By 1980, global vaccination had eliminated smallpox entirely. It's the only human disease we've completely eradicated.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Herd Protection
q3.script: When enough people are vaccinated, diseases can't spread—even to those who can't be vaccinated. This 'herd immunity' protects entire communities. Individual vaccination is also collective protection.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Preparation beats reaction. Vaccines prove that training before battle determines outcomes. Your immune system is powerful, but it's even more powerful when it knows what's coming.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 127. Tomorrow, we'll explore fixing the body from inside—surgery. Until then, appreciate that your immune system can learn—and that we've found ways to teach it.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Immune Appreciation - Know Your Defenders
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate your immune system's learning ability
growTrack.activity: Consider which vaccinations you've had. Each one trained your immune system against a specific threat. Your body now has memory cells ready to fight enemies you've never actually encountered. Preparation is protection.
